text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers.
DER STANDARD
- Austria's government plans another 25 billion to 50 billion schillings in budget cuts until the year 2000 in order to keep its deficit in line with Maastricht criteria for European Monetary Union.
- Flag-carrier Austrian Airlines expects to report a full-year pretax profit despite sharp losses in the first half.
- Insolvencies to rise 10 percent to a record 5,400 this year, study says.
- Savings bank Die Erste leaves its options open in the race for government sell-off candidate Creditanstalt.
DIE PRESSE
- First day of inscription for Vienna univeristy's winter term marred by chaos and long lines
- Talks between Social Democrat Labour Affairs Minister Franz Hums and conservative Family Minister Martin Bartenstein over new labour contract laws have ended in disagreement.
- Steyr Daimler Puch to introduce more flexible working hours in a bid to cut costs.
- Austria needs more exporters, says chamber of commerce's foreign trade director.
- Finance Minister Viktor Klima says he is in favour of including employment targets in the European Union Treaty ahead of Europe's planned monetary union.
KURIER
- Number of registered allegations of child abuse has risen 53 percent in the first six months of the year.
- Long-term unemployment has risen dramatically, forcing 81,000 Austrians to live on state emergency benefits -- up 17 percent from last year.
- Austria pledges to award license for a third mobile phone network before the year 1998.
- As many as 51 percent of Austrians are confident about the country's economic prospects, up from 43 percent in May, a new study shows.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Switzerland's Swatch group plans to set up a production facility in Austria.
- An Austro-German-Italian consortium bidding for Creditanstalt now say they want Die Erste savings bank back in their group.
